title: Prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy
requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (software that uses nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old to recommend rents, fees, occupancy or other lease terms) when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units, and no one may sell, license or provide such an algorithm to Berkeley landlords. This amending ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025; the document does not state the final adoption or effective date.
key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)
coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley; applies to landlords using and to vendors selling or licensing coordinated pricing algorithms.
exemptions: Not covered: reports publishing aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines; information used for project-financing market research, appraisals, or software research, testing or training (if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated). The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
citation: Berkeley Mun. Code Ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S.
